summary: Iter-7 testing: Worker approval gate (pending/approved/rejected/suspended/reinstate) + Recurring gigs (daily/weekly/biweekly/monthly with repeat_count, series_id). Created 24 new backend tests in test_iter7.py — ALL 24 PASS. Updated shared `_make_verified_worker` helpers in backend_test.py, test_calendar.py, test_iter5.py, test_iter6.py to also call /admin/workers/{id}/approve (workers default to 'pending' now, accept gate requires both ID verification AND status=approved). Also fixed test_iter6's `test_no_id_uploaded_blocks_accept` and `test_uploaded_but_unverified_blocks_accept` to approve worker first so the ID gate is reached. Total backend pytest suite: 115 passed (91 prior + 24 new). Frontend UI testing confirmed: AdminWorkers 5 status tabs work and URL updates with ?status=pending, application-status-card + Approve/Reject buttons present on /admin/workers/{id}, CreateGigDialog has gig-recurrence dropdown with gig-repeat-count conditionally shown. HOWEVER one major frontend gap was found: AdminDashboard is MISSING the 'Pending apps' KPI tile AND the yellow strip with data-testid='dashboard-pending-apps-link'. Dashboard still shows only 4 tiles (Open gigs / Filled / Workers / Pending ID).

ui_bugs.issue: 'Pending apps' KPI tile is MISSING. Dashboard renders only 4 tiles (Open gigs / Filled / Workers / Pending ID) and never displays pending_approval count from /admin/stats. Required by iter-7 spec.

Yellow strip with data-testid='dashboard-pending-apps-link' is MISSING. When pending_approval > 0 the dashboard should display a yellow strip that navigates to /admin/workers?status=pending. Not rendered at all.

action_items: Add the 'Pending apps' KPI tile to AdminDashboard.jsx that displays stats.pending_approval (use the same KPI component pattern).
Add the yellow strip with data-testid='dashboard-pending-apps-link' below the KPI row, only when stats.pending_approval > 0, that on click navigates to /admin/workers?status=pending.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1467 lines — getting close to the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting recurrence logic, worker-status helpers, and admin endpoints into dedicated modules in a future iteration.
_set_worker_status helper correctly persists worker_status_at + worker_status_by and kills sessions for reject/suspend — well factored.
Recurrence math uses naive month arithmetic with clamping to last day of month — covered by tests; behavior matches spec.
Back-compat for users without worker_status field handled via _effective_status helper and list filter includes legacy users in 'approved' — verified.
